aAbout: Maltego is an OSINT and cyber investigations platform built around visual link analysis. Its flagship, Maltego Graph, lets investigators expand entities — people, domains, companies, digital identifiers — into relationship graphs, on the desktop for large-scale investigations and in the browser via Maltego One with built-in data, map and histogram views and an AI Assistant. Around the graph sit Maltego Search for quick OSINT lookups, Maltego Monitor for real-time social media monitoring, Maltego Evidence for preserving social media evidence, plus Cases and Admin. Data arrives through curated Maltego Data Pass sources, 100+ Connectors driven by the user's own API keys, and a Connector Builder and Transforms SDK for proprietary sources.
aStrengths: Maltego is the deeper investigation instrument: a mature graph canvas designed for large, multifaceted cases, automated expansion across curated commercial and OSINT data, Search for person-of-interest lookups, Monitor for live social listening, and Evidence and Hunchly capture for material that may need a chain of custody. Its connector ecosystem — 100+ integrations, a builder and an SDK — means an organisation's own data can join the graph, and training, support and ISO 27001:2022 certification signal a platform built for professional and government teams.
bAbout: Intelligence X, at intelx.io, is a search engine and data archive — in its own words, it indexes data from public sources and is data agnostic. Its indexed buckets include paste sites (including historical ones), Tor and I2P darknet content, Wikileaks and Cryptome, government sites, data leaks, whois data and the public web, searchable only by selector — an email, domain, IP or CIDR, Bitcoin address, phone number and similar strong identifiers. Full-text search is explicitly not supported. It also keeps historical copies of websites and documents, offers a Phonebook for finding a strong selector from an incomplete one, and sells an Identity Portal for leaked-account and reverse-lookup work on higher tiers. Its own pages conflict on dataset size — 200 billion records on the product page, about 400 billion in an October 2026 blog post — so the honest summary is hundreds of billions claimed.
bStrengths: Intelligence X is the deeper archive: few tools let you query darknet, leak, paste-site, whois and historical web material from one selector search, view archived documents inline without leaving the site, and set alerts for when new material matching a selector appears. Its Phonebook solves the common problem of not knowing the full identifier, free use is genuinely available — 2 searches a day logged out, 50 a day signed up — and documented Search and Leaks APIs plus a Maltego integration make it a building block in wider investigation toolchains.
betterAnswer: They do different OSINT jobs. Maltego maps relationships: start from one entity and build a graph of what connects to what, across curated and commercial data. Intelligence X finds records: start from a selector and retrieve what the archive holds across darknet, leaks, pastes and historical copies. An investigation often needs both in sequence — find records in Intelligence X, then map the relationships they reveal in Maltego, which is why Intelligence X is also reachable from inside Maltego's ecosystem.
consA: Real data depth starts at €3,000/yr — the free tier is credit-limited
A Maltego ID is required, and paid plans are subject to vetting
No mobile app found on its official pages
Graph work has a learning curve beside a simple search box
Advanced Monitor and Evidence are Enterprise options
consB: No full-text search — you must already know a selector
Paid licences are yearly only, starting at €3,000/yr
Dataset size conflicts on its own pages (200B vs 400B records)
No graph or link-analysis view of results
No desktop or mobile app mentioned on its official pages

faqs.a: No — they do different jobs. Maltego is a link-analysis platform: it visualises relationships between entities on a graph. Intelligence X is a selector-based search engine and archive: it retrieves records for an email, domain, IP or other identifier. Intelligence X data can also be reached from within Maltego's ecosystem, so the two are often used together.
faqs.q: Is Maltego the same kind of tool as Intelligence X?

faqs.a: Partly. The Basic Community Edition is €0/year with Maltego Graph and 200 Maltego Credits per month, and Basic+ is €0/year for qualified users (1,000 credits per month; registration with an official government or organisational email is required to be considered). A Maltego ID is required either way, and paid plans — Entry Standard €3,000/year, Professional Standard €7,500/year — are subject to Maltego's vetting process. Prices here are the EUR figures shown on the official pricing page; USD figures are unverified.

Yes, within limits. With no login you get 2 selector searches a day; a free signed-up account gets 50 a day, and new accounts receive a 7-day free trial (50 searches a day, with some data buckets such as leaks and stealer logs reserved for paid users). Paid licences are yearly only: Researcher €3,000/year, API €7,000/year, Identity Portal €10,000/year and Enterprise €20,000/year.

No. Intelligence X states plainly that full-text searches are not supported — you search for a selector such as a domain, email address, IP address or Bitcoin address. If you only have a partial identifier, its Phonebook service is designed to help you find the strong selector first.
faqs.q: Can Intelligence X do full-text search?

faqs.a: Intelligence X claims hundreds of billions of records, but its own pages disagree on the exact figure: the product page says more than 200 billion records, while an official blog post dated 23 October 2026 puts the dataset at about 400 billion. We do not quote a single hard number because the official sources conflict.
faqs.q: How big is the Intelligence X dataset?

faqs.a: Neither replaces the other. Maltego Graph is included in every Maltego plan, on desktop and in the browser via Maltego One. Intelligence X is web and APIs only, but it is also available as an integration within investigation toolchains — including a Maltego transform via its public SDK — so archive results can feed graph work.

intro: Maltego and Intelligence X are both serious OSINT tools, but they start investigations from opposite ends. Maltego is a link-analysis platform: give it an entity and it draws the graph of what connects to it, across curated data, commercial sources and 100+ connectors. Intelligence X is a search engine and data archive: give it a selector — an email, domain, IP, Bitcoin address — and it retrieves what its index holds across darknet, leaks, paste sites, whois and historical copies. Mapping relationships versus finding records: different jobs, often done in that order.

verdictA: Choose Maltego if your job is mapping relationships — building an evidence-backed graph of people, companies and digital footprints for a case, and pivoting across commercial and curated data to do it.
verdictB: Choose Intelligence X if your job is finding records — checking whether a selector appears in darknet, leak, paste, whois or historical material, with an archive deep enough that a negative result means something.
verdictLine: Maltego answers 'what is this connected to?'; Intelligence X answers 'where has this appeared?'. Serious investigations ask both questions — which is why the archive feeds the graph in real toolchains, rather than one tool replacing the other.
worldEye: WorldEye is not a third answer to this contest, and it does not pretend to be: it is a live-world viewing and OSINT-search tool, not a Maltego-grade link-analysis platform or an Intelligence X-grade archive. What it does is show the world as it is now — a free 3D globe with no signup, 74,229 public cameras across 105 countries, live flights, ships, weather and events — which can ground an investigation geographically once Maltego or Intelligence X has produced the lead. Its Pro tier is $7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year.
